counterevidence_considered.description: Strongest candidate for the issue: both samples are extracted from the same staged rows, which could superficially suggest shared structure; however the task declares the row pairing a storage convention only and no identifier repeats, so no repeated-unit entry occurs.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: no duplicated k1 or k2 code

source_refs.quoted_text:
left = [float(row["a"]) for row in staged]
right = [float(row["b"]) for row in staged]

Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. The table stores two disjoint collections of source items. `k1` identifies a first-collection source item measured by column `a`; `k2` identifies a second-collection source item measured by column `b`. The two collections are disjoint. `tag` is an opaque annotation. The row pairing is a storage convention only; there is no matching, pairing, block, or other relationship between the `k1` item and the `k2` item in that row.

evidence.description: Every k1 identifier (u01–u12) and every k2 identifier appears exactly once across the 12 staged rows, so no source item enters the procedure more than once.
evidence.observed_value: 12 rows, 12 distinct k1 codes, 12 distinct k2 codes

evidence.description: The applied procedure is an unpaired, row-independent rank test over the two disjoint samples; with unique units per row this matches the stated data structure.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the negative verdict by scanning all 12 rows for any repeated k1 code, repeated k2 code, or duplicated full row, and by checking whether the reported statistic implies an inflated sample count. All identifiers are distinct, and a Mann-Whitney U of 60.5 with p=0.524 is consistent with 12-vs-12 samples. No route to demonstrating repeated unit entry survived.
